Tracking Data

For a number of the questions, the tracking findings from the 1997 Environmental Monitor Survey as well as the 1992 "Health of the Planet" survey conducted by the Gallup International Institute were reported.

Geographical Region

The countries that are studied in this report have been grouped both regionally and by per capita purchasing power to aid in understanding global patterns. The seven regional groupings are:

  • Africa: Nigeria and South Africa
  • Asia: China, India, Indonesia, Japan and Korea
  • Eastern Europe / Central Asia: Hungary, Kazakhstan, Poland, and Russia
  • Latin America: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, and Venezuela
  • Mediterranean: Greece, Italy, Spain, and Turkey
  • North America / Oceania: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United States
  • Northern Europe: Finland, France, Germany, and Great Britain
Gross Domestic Product

There are three equal groupings of ten countries each based on their Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita (called "purchasing power parity"):

  • High GDP per capita (US$28,600-$18,500): United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Finland, and New Zealand (in decreasing order)
  • Medium GDP per capita (US$15,300-$6,400): Spain, South Korea, Greece, Venezuela, Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Uruguay, Hungary, and Poland
  • Low GDP per capita (US$6,300-$1,380): Brazil, Turkey, Colombia, South Africa, Russia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, China, India, and Nigeria
Psychographic Segmentation

A Psychographic segmentation has also been created dividing people in all countries into various segments depending on the nature of their engagement with environmental issues and concerns.

Figures and Charts

All figures ad charts in this report are expressed in percentages. Total percentages may not add up because of rounding.

Environics International Environmental Monitors (EIEM) is a syndicated annual survey of global public opinion on a variety of environmental and natural resource issues. The findings of the 1998 Survey are based on the results of face-to face or telephone interviews with representative samples of about 1,000 citizens, in each of 30 countries on all continents, representing over 68 percent of the world's population. Research was conducted by respected social research institutes in each country between January 21, 1998 and May 26, 1998. A total of 47 questions were posed dealing with such topics as overall environmental concerns, possible human health impacts, seriousness of specific environmental problems, action alternatives on climate change, energy concerns and preferences, perceived benefits vs. risks of modern technology, agricultural chemicals and biotechnology, and assessments of the environmental performance of various industry sectors.
